name: Registered Valuer
title: Registered Valuer (IBBI)
intro: From the right degree to an IBBI Registered Valuer: experience as the Rules require, RVO membership and its 50-hour course, the IBBI valuation exam for your asset class, then registration and yearly continuing education.

phases.title: Get the right degree
phases.summary: Matched to the asset class you want.
points: CA/CS/CMA/MBA-finance for securities or financial assets.
Civil engineering or architecture for land & building.

phases.title: Build experience
phases.summary: In valuation, audit, engineering or finance, as the Rules require.
points: The Companies (Registered Valuers and Valuation) Rules, 2017 set the minimum years of experience for each qualification.
Experience can come from valuation, audit, engineering or finance work.
Valuation advisory teams in consulting firms offer salaried roles.

phases.title: Join an RVO and take its course
phases.summary: IBBI publishes the list of recognised Registered Valuers Organisations.
points: The course certificate is uploaded when you enrol for the exam.

phases.title: IBBI valuation exam
phases.summary: Separate exams for each asset class.
points: Separate exams for land & building, plant & machinery, and securities or financial assets.
IBBI publishes and regularly reviews the curriculum for each asset class.
You can register in more than one class if you meet the eligibility and pass each exam.

phases.title: Register and practise
phases.summary: Register with IBBI, then practise with continuing education every year.
points: Apply to IBBI for registration, then complete continuing education every year.
Work comes from insolvency professionals, companies, banks, courts and tribunals; most valuers earn per valuation report.
Often combined with CA/CMA practice, engineering consultancy or real-estate advisory; complex insolvency and M&A valuations pay well.
